hypotheses.justification: The proof only needs it for `continuousAt_of_dominated`, which requires a countably generated filter. A direct uniform-continuity proof avoids it. Fix x₀ and ε>0 and pick δ>0 with δ·(μ s).toReal < ε. `IsCompact.mem_uniformity_of_prod` (Topology/UniformSpace/HeineCantor.lean), applied with s := univ, k := s, hf.continuousOn and `dist_mem_uniformity`, gives a neighbourhood V of x₀ with ‖f x y - f x₀ y‖ < δ for all x ∈ V and y ∈ s. This is the tube lemma and needs nothing about X beyond its topology. Each f x is continuous, hence AEStronglyMeasurable (`Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable`, using the OpensMeasurableSpace Y and SecondCountableTopologyEither Y E instances, which stay). It is bounded on compact s (`IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn`), and μ s < ∞ (`hs.measure_ne_top`), so it is integrable on s. Then `integral_sub` and `norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const` give ‖∫_s f x - ∫_s f x₀‖ ≤ δ·(μ s).toReal < ε for x ∈ V. The neighbouring lemma `continuousOn_integral_bilinear_of_locally_integrable_of_compact_support` is proved this way with no extra assumption on X. Degenerate cases (μ s = 0, s or X empty) are harmless. This can be deleted on its own, or together with [LocallyCompactSpace X].

The proof only needs it for `exists_compact_mem_nhds x₀`, which gives a compact neighbourhood on which ‖f‖ is bounded, the dominating constant for `continuousAt_of_dominated`. The uniform-continuity argument needs no such neighbourhood. `IsCompact.mem_uniformity_of_prod` (applied to hf.continuousOn on univ ×ˢ s, using compactness of s only) gives a neighbourhood V of x₀ on which sup_{y∈s} ‖f x y - f x₀ y‖ < δ. Integrability of each f x on s comes from continuity plus `Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable`, boundedness on compact s and `hs.measure_ne_top`. Then `norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const` bounds the difference of the integrals by δ·(μ s).toReal, which proves continuity at x₀. This can be deleted on its own, or together with [FirstCountableTopology X].
